tweet_summary: Doctor account shows an animated anatomy video about nasal/sinus irrigation with saline rinse, captioned 'This is how you actually clear your sinuses'. 20.8M views.
why_note_decision: The video shows mainstream, medically-accepted information about nasal saline irrigation — it's standard ENT care for rhinosinusitis (one top reply even says exactly that). The tweet itself doesn't claim anything false. The original CN note adds a safety reminder (use distilled/sterile/boiled water, not tap, to avoid rare Naegleria infections) — which is good advice but isn't correcting a misleading claim. Adding supplementary safety advice is not the same as correcting misinformation. Dominant rater feedback was 'note not needed' (5).
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet/video accurately depicts standard medical practice for sinus irrigation; the only thing to add would be a safety reminder (use distilled/sterile/boiled-cooled water), but that's supplementary safety info, not a correction of a false claim. fact_check.claim_verdict: Video depicts standard, medically-accepted nasal-irrigation practice; no false claim to correct.
fact_check.notes: Saline nasal irrigation is standard care for sinusitis. CDC/FDA do recommend distilled/sterile/boiled water to avoid Naegleria — a valid safety reminder, but the tweet doesn't claim tap water is fine, so there's no misleading claim to correct.
